canonical_name: Riemannian positive mass theorem in dimension three
canonical_statement: For a complete, connected, asymptotically flat Riemannian three-manifold without boundary and with nonnegative scalar curvature, the ADM mass of each selected asymptotically flat end is nonnegative; if that mass is zero, the manifold is isometric to Euclidean three-space.
domain_and_universes: A smooth connected Riemannian manifold of real dimension 3 with a selected asymptotically flat end; exact Lean universes, regularity, and decay structures are not frozen
quantifiers: (M, g): complete connected smooth Riemannian 3-manifold without boundary
E: a selected asymptotically flat end of (M, g)
m_ADM(E): the ADM mass defined using the asymptotic chart and decay hypotheses
hypotheses: the scalar curvature of g is nonnegative
the metric is asymptotically flat with the regularity and decay needed to define invariant ADM mass
the hypotheses required by the selected primary-source formulation hold
conclusion: m_ADM(E) >= 0, and m_ADM(E) = 0 implies (M, g) is isometric to Euclidean three-space
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: The nonnegativity assertion and zero-mass rigidity are both in scope; an inequality-only surrogate is not the complete root
The general Lorentzian initial-data theorem with nonzero second fundamental form is excluded
Manifolds with horizons or compact boundary, charged or asymptotically hyperbolic variants, and dimensions other than three are excluded
A coordinate formula on Euclidean space is not a substitute for chart independence or the geometric theorem
